title: Author + implement PROP-082: make workspace-sync's universal-pusher policy-aware so it stops re-adding files prune deleted (break the prune ↔ workspace-sync re-add loop)
background:
Tinker's 2026-06-07T02-40 report flagged finding F1 [major]: prune ↔ workspace-sync re-add loop. Pruned files resurrect within ~16 minutes of every daily prune run. Retention never converges. Empirically verified 2026-06-07T05:50Z operator inspection:

  - Yesterday's prune (commit b8e3c000 at 08:06:24Z) deleted 1,440 files including monitor/integrity/narrative-cite-audit-2026-05-17T*.json (42 days old, deep past the 7-day retention).
  - Workspace-sync's next cycle (commit 73f18678 at 08:22:18Z, 16 min later) RE-ADDED them via universal-pusher rescue.
  - All 23 of the 2026-05-17 narrative-cite-audit files are HTTP 200 on origin/main right now (12 hours after deletion).
  - The integrity directory currently holds 892 files vs the expected ~20-170 per retention policy. The historical accumulation from ~6 weeks of unconverged retention.

Mechanism (confirmed by tinker forensics):

  1. Prune deletes files from git via its clone push.
  2. FUSE cannot unlink() (chronic constraint documented in CLAUDE.md). FUSE copies of the pruned files persist forever.
  3. workspace-sync runs hourly. Its universal-pusher logic sees 'file in FUSE, not in git' and pushes it back as rescue.
  4. Files resurrect ~16 minutes later. Daily prune scans the same files next morning, deletes them, churn repeats.
  5. Archive JSONLs (narrative-cite-audit-archive.jsonl etc.) get duplicate entries appended every cycle, growing unboundedly with dupes.
  6. Tracker rebuilds: ~1,400 files/day delete-and-re-add work for both prune and workspace-sync (confirmed across 06-04 = 1,348, 06-06 = 1,440).

Same defect family as the unactioned DIRECTIVE-20260521-002 (audit-files no-round-trip). Different surface but same root cause: pusher cannot distinguish 'workflow-deleted, do not rescue' from 'agent-authored, please rescue'.

TIMING: today's prune is scheduled for ~08:06Z (~2h 15min from filing time). If PROP-082 ships before then, the next workspace-sync rescue after prune will skip the deleted files and the loop is broken on this cycle. Operator will manually run tinker to ship before that deadline; cron tinker is daily 03:30 PT (10:30 UTC) which is AFTER prune.

operator_decision.rationale: Tinker's recommendation (a) — make workspace-sync's universal-pusher policy-aware — is the structurally correct fix. Reuses the existing parseFilenameTimestamp helper + the policies table from prune-integrity.js. No new manifest file to maintain. The deny-list-from-prune alternative (b) creates coupling between two agents and adds a file the universal-pusher must consult. Option (a) is cleaner.

requested_work: Step 1 — Read monitor/scripts/prune-integrity.js to extract the policies table (the per-category retention rules: workspace-sync-runs, verify-pending-run, narrative-cite-audit, push-failure, report-daily, abort, divergence, sync-workspace-runs, non-ff-abort). Document the rules in PROP-082's evidence section. Reuse the parseFilenameTimestamp helper that already exists.

Step 2 — Read monitor/prompts/workspace-sync.md to locate the universal-pusher logic (the section that pushes runtime data files from FUSE to git when FUSE has newer content). Identify the exact decision point where 'file-in-FUSE-absent-in-git' triggers the push.

Step 3 — Author monitor/tinker/proposals/PROP-082-universal-pusher-policy-aware.json. Required sections: title, problem statement (cite this directive + tinker's F1 finding + the empirical loop forensics), proposed fix (the policy-aware filter), Q-OPs if any, verification_pattern (grep + simulation against the 23 narrative-cite-audit-2026-05-17 files), files_touched list, estimated_loc.

Step 4 — Implement the policy-aware filter. Operator pre-approves the following design direction: extend workspace-sync's universal-pusher with a pre-check that parses the filename's embedded timestamp + matches against the prune-integrity policies table. If the file's timestamp is OLDER than the retention window for its category, SKIP the push (log to workspace-sync-skips.jsonl with reason 'older-than-prune-retention'). Otherwise, proceed with the normal rescue logic. The filter only fires for files matching the categories in the policies table; files outside those categories (e.g., monitor/decisions/open-issues.json) are unaffected and still get rescued as before. Keep the policies table inline in workspace-sync.md OR import it from prune-integrity.js's exported structure — tinker picks based on cleaner LOC budget.

Step 5 — Tinker self-applies per the PROP-076/077/078/079/080/081 pattern: write proposal, implement same run if total LOC <100 across workspace-sync.md + any helper extracted, verification simulation passes for all 23 narrative-cite-audit-2026-05-17 files (the filter should refuse to push each one).

Step 6 — Validation: simulate the 2026-06-06T08:06→08:22 timeline. After implementing the filter, the next universal-pusher run AFTER a prune deletion should NOT re-add files older than the retention window. Use the 23 narrative-cite-audit-2026-05-17 files as the canary set. Each should hit the new skip-by-policy filter. Document outcomes in PROP-082's verification section. Include `workspace-sync-skips.jsonl` example output showing the new skip reason.

Step 7 — Lifecycle: flip PROP-082.json status='implemented' with implementation_commit/at/run. Flip this directive to status='completed' with prop_id_implemented set. Reference back to tinker's F1 finding in the proposal (it was the surfacing report).

Step 8 — Manually copy edited workspace-sync.md (and any imported policies helper if extracted) to FUSE so the next workspace-sync run picks up the new logic. dome-mirror will propagate within ~30 min on its :30 cron, but manual sync is the safe bootstrap path before today's 08:06Z prune.

Step 9 — Post-deployment canary plan: after today's 08:06Z prune fires, verify the 09:09Z workspace-sync cycle does NOT re-add the deleted files. If even ONE pruned file resurrects, the filter has a hole and needs immediate amendment. Tinker should write this expectation into PROP-082's post-deployment plan; operator monitors the 09:09Z cycle.

Step 10 — DIRECTIVE-20260521-002 cross-reference: this PROP closes part of that older directive's scope (it was the same defect family). PROP-082's proposal should mention that DIRECTIVE-20260521-002's 'audit-files round-trip' surface is the adjacent case that remains unactioned; not in scope here but worth noting for future work.
non_goals: Do NOT modify monitor/scripts/prune-integrity.js's deletion logic. Prune works correctly; only the rescue layer needs the policy-aware filter.
Do NOT implement deny-list approach (b). Operator pre-approved (a). The deny-list creates inter-agent coupling and an additional file to maintain.
Do NOT broaden the universal-pusher filter to other categories (decision files, analyst tracker, etc.). Stay scoped to the categories in prune-integrity.js's policies table.

Do NOT attempt to retroactively delete the ~5,000 files already accumulated in monitor/integrity/. The operator-side allow_cowork_file_delete + rm sweep is a separate decision; PROP-082 only fixes the forward-looking loop. Once the loop is broken, the next 5-7 days of normal prune cycles will catch up.
Do NOT touch dome-mirror's git→FUSE propagation logic. The FUSE-cannot-unlink constraint is upstream of this fix; dome-mirror is not the bug.
Do NOT supersede PROP-077 / PROP-078 (those fixed FUSE-revert race; different surface). PROP-082 is parallel work on the universal-pusher's filter logic.

Do NOT scope to fixing DIRECTIVE-20260521-002's audit-files round-trip case in this run. Same defect family but different file shapes (audit files have multiple-write patterns); needs its own proposal.
